copies.headline: Kaleb's Skill Positions Clocked Out Entirely
copies.body:
The running backs ended this before halftime. Noah got 40.3 from James Cook III and Rhamondre Stevenson; Kaleb got 11.4 from Ashton Jeanty and RJ Harvey, who contributed 0.7 points and presumably a hand towel. Add Drake Maye's 39.5 and Noah had 80 points from three roster spots, which is 80 more than Kaleb's entire flex-tight end-WR2 combination mustered. Carnell Tate (1.6 on 13.5 projected), Harold Fannin Jr. (1.4 on 12.0) and Jordan Addison (0.0, with Keenan Allen and Tre Tucker both watching from the bench) is not a lineup, it's a hostage situation.
Kaleb's defense won by 15 and his kicker lost by 10.7, which tells you how little the margins mattered. Noah even started the Cowboys D/ST for negative two with the Browns scoring 11 on his bench and still won by 55.6. We picked Noah by eight; he beat the number by seven touchdowns.
Noah's 141.3 is his season high by 31, which moves him to 1-4 and absolutely nowhere in the standings — but the postseason assassin has started slower than this before. Kaleb drops to 3-2 with a 38% all-play, which is the polite way of saying he's been getting away with it.

copies.headline: John's Tight Ends Alone Beat CJ's Receivers
copies.body:
The game was over at tight end, twice. Trey McBride went for 21.6 and Brock Bowers added 23.0 out of the flex, giving John 44 and change from the position CJ addressed with Juwan Johnson's 5.6. That's a 16-point hole at TE and another 9.8 at flex before anyone looks at Puka Nacua's 37.7, which was more than CJ got from his entire receiver room. John won every position but kicker.
CJ's problem wasn't effort, it was the middle of his lineup collapsing at once. Jonathan Taylor managed 11.2 against a 19.0 projection, DK Metcalf put up 5.3 on a 12.3 projection, and Emeka Egbuka's 17.2 sat on the bench watching. Parker Washington's 30.4 was a genuinely great week that mattered to nobody.
John's at 3-2 with a 37-18 all-play, second in scoring, and a 172.7 season high that says the power ranking wasn't flattery. We called it by 13; he beat the spread by 47. CJ falls back toward the line he's lived under for four years.

copies.headline: Raiders Defense Hands Grant the Game
copies.body:
Isaac won the skill positions and lost anyway. He took QB by 0.4, running back by 8.1, receiver by 3.6 — and then started the Raiders defense, which scored minus six. That's a 15-point swing against Cincinnati's unit in a game decided by 11.9. Add T.J. Hockenson's 1.7 on a 10.5 projection, and the hole was dug before Grant's lineup even had to do anything clever.
Grant didn't do anything clever. Tony Pollard managed 5.2 on 13.6, Quinshon Judkins 8.0 on 14.6, Amon-Ra St. Brown 12.9 on a 20.0 projection, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt put up 14.2 on the bench. Christian Watson's 32.3 and Jacoby Brissett's 25.3 covered all of it. Malik Nabers went for 29.1 in a loss, which is the Isaac experience in one line.
We picked Isaac by 9 and the defense ate the pick. He's 2-3, 11th in scoring, 16-39 in all-play, and still somehow a half-win luckier than he's earned. Grant is 3-2 by vibes and variance, exactly on brand.

copies.headline: Adam's Backfield Buries Peter In The Basement
copies.body:
The running backs decided it before anything else did. Bucky Irving went for 31.5 and Peter's entire backfield — Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. — mustered 17.4 combined, a 19.9-point hole on its own. Add the kicker gap (Will Reichard 16.9, Evan McPherson 6.6) and the Jets defense outscoring Washington's 18.0 to 3.0, and Peter was down roughly 45 at the positions nobody thinks about on Sunday morning. Jayden Daniels' 32.3 and Sam LaPorta's 19.8 just made the arithmetic rude.
Peter's starters quit on him in a group. Romeo Doubs 2.6 against a 12.2 projection, Tee Higgins 4.2 on 12.8, Brian Robinson 1.6 on 8.1. Worse, Denzel Boston put up 13.6 on the bench and Roschon Johnson 9.0, which is 20-plus points of lineup error — not enough to touch 161.8, but enough to make 95.4 look like a choice.
We had Adam by 16; he got there four times over. He's 5-0 with a 49-6 all-play and the league's best scoring average, which is the boring kind of dominance. Peter drops to 4-1 with +1.5 luck wins — the 2022 ghost still isn't walking.

copies.headline: Rezac's Back End Was a Disaster and He Won Anyway
copies.body:
Logan won this on the spine. Joe Burrow's 24.6 beat Dak Prescott by twelve, Jaylen Warren's 36.8 and Braelon Allen's 18.6 gave him a 55.4-to-40.7 edge at running back, and Isaiah Likely's 32.4 at tight end was eleven more than Tyler Warren. That's roughly 38 points of advantage from three spots, which is exactly how much Logan needed, because his kicker and defense combined for literally nothing — Chad Ryland 2.0, Bears D/ST minus-2. Mitchell got 27.3 from Tyler Loop and the Broncos and still lost.
The bench bills nearly came due. Jeremiyah Love scored 2.2 on a 14.4 projection in the flex while MarShawn Lloyd put up 16.7 in street clothes. Mitchell's was worse: Konata Mumpfield's zero with Xavier Hutchinson (10.5) and Courtland Sutton (9.8) available. Jahmyr Gibbs' 37.7 deserved better than Rachaad White's 3.0.
Both sit 1-4 with negative luck, which is the honest read — Mitchell's the human coin flip, Logan's the guy who keeps scoring and losing. Our preview had Mitchell by 13. It did not age.

copies.headline: Leif's Receivers Buried Christian Before Kickoff Cooled
copies.body:
Wideouts decided this one and it wasn't close. Davante Adams and Mike Evans combined for 48.4 while Christian's pair managed 21.6 — a 26.8-point hole dug by CeeDee Lamb's 2.9 on a 19.1 projection. Add Jason Myers somehow kicking 25 points and Leif had a 46-point edge from two positions nobody drafts with conviction. Christian actually won the flex by 10.5 and the tight end spot by 1.4, which is the fantasy equivalent of winning the coin toss.
The misses compound: Chase Brown at 7.0 on 17.4, George Kittle at 7.4 on 13.7, and Khalil Shakir's 11 points sitting on the bench behind Lamb. Leif had his own disaster in David Montgomery's 1.1 with Kyle Pitts' 15.2 idling, and it cost him nothing.
Christian is 1-4 with the fourth-best scoring average and an all-play of 31-24, which means the record is a lie but the loss isn't. Leif, career 22-34, is 3-2 and legitimately third in all-play. We picked Christian by 11; file that one away.

intro: Four of six games were decided by 55 points or more, which is less a slate than a culling — Adam hung 161.76 on Peter, Leif put up 164.3 on Christian, and John's 172.72 was the week's high-water mark and also CJ's problem. The only real football happened in the margins: Logan survived Mitchell 142.3 to 132.94, and Grant held off Isaac by 11.94 in a game neither roster seemed especially interested in winning. If you scored under 110 this week, you weren't unlucky, you were just there.
